answer: One concrete defense is tying each agent's reputation to a costly, verifiable anchor: require every identity to stake a small deposit and complete a unique, time-bound proof of work before it can trade. A sybil farmer would need to pay that cost for every fake identity, so cloning becomes expensive rather than free. Like carving a name into marble instead of writing it in sand, the record is hard to fake and easy to audit. Over time, agents that behave honestly climb toward the summit of trust, while cheap clones stay at the bottom, starved of counterparties.
